DOCTOR VISIT LESSON · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Medicine — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the medicine rule that outlives every visit: medicine helps the body heal, and it is taken only from a grown-up — measured and given by them, every time.

What is this?

Medicine is what helps a sick body get better — the doctor or pharmacist says how much, and a grown-up gives it exactly that way.

What does it mean?

Children learn rules as sentences they can recite. "Only from a grown-up" is short, true, and repeated at every medicine moment until the child is the one saying it.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and the rule, said the same way every time: grown-ups measure it, grown-ups give it. Real medicine lives up high. Toy medicine stays pretend. No exceptions, stated kindly.

Why this matters

This is the safety line of the whole set. Medicine mistakes at home are real and preventable, and the prevention is a three-year-old who recites the rule without being asked.

What it teaches

Safety rules as recitable sentences, the distinction between medicine and candy (same shelf, different rules), and the child&rsquo;s role: asking first, always.

Words to learn

medicinegrown-uprulemeasuredoseheal

Say this to your child

“"Medicine! Take it only from a grown-up. Grown-ups measure it, grown-ups give it — and then it helps your body do its healing work."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and read its words together: "take it only from a grown-up."
  2. The two-part rule: "grown-ups measure it, grown-ups give it."
  3. Practice asking: "may I have my medicine?" — the asking is the child&rsquo;s job.
  4. Where medicine lives: up high, away from toys, never in the play kitchen.
  5. Say the rule at every real medicine moment — the child repeats the last half.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "medicine — take it only from a grown-up" sit over a grown-up giving a child a small medicine cup while a teddy bear watches.

Ask your child

"Who gives medicine?" (only a grown-up) "What do you say if you want it?" (may I have my medicine, please) "Is medicine candy?" (never — it is medicine, with its own rules)

What your child can say or do

Your child might recite the rule to grandma unprompted, "prescribe" pretend medicine with perfect rules, or catch a toy rule-breaker and correct them sternly.

Out in the real world

Vitamin gummies, cough syrup, grandma&rsquo;s pills — all medicine, all grown-up-given. The rule does not bend for candy-shaped anything.

Try it together

Pharmacy Rules: the play store sells "medicine" boxes, and every sale requires the buyer to say the rule out loud — "only from a grown-up!" No recitation, no sale. The rule becomes the game’s currency.

Understanding check

Ask: "Who gives you medicine?" (a grown-up — only) "What do you say first?" (may I have my medicine) "Is medicine a treat?" (no — it is healing, with rules)

Staying safe

If medicine ever looks like candy, the rule still wins — and the medicine moves higher. When the child recites it unprompted, celebrate it like a diploma.

This lesson pairs with the Medicine flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Doctor Visit.
